title: Harry Styles & Thom Yorke | Musicians on Musicians

phrases.en: - Do you travel with a laptop? - My laptop has been dead for about six years. I don't know where the charger is. - We can help you with - That.
phrases.ja: ノートパソコン、旅に持っていく？ 僕のパソコン、6年くらい死んでる。充電器がどこかも分からない。それなら手伝えるよ。それ。

phrases.en: I know. We met for the first time in Rome on a small street. - Yes. - You were playing in Rome that week with the smile. Yeah.
phrases.ja: 知ってる。初めて会ったの、ローマの細い道だった。うん。その週、The Smileでローマに出てた。うん。

phrases.en: So I'd just been talking about... I was going to that show. Was it before the show? It was before the show. Yeah.
phrases.ja: だからちょうど話してたんだ。あのショーに行くって。ショーの前？ 前だった。うん。

phrases.en: And a friend of mine had asked me if we'd ever met and I had said that we hadn't.
phrases.ja: 友達に、会ったことある？って聞かれて、ない、って言ってた。

phrases.en: So I was walking down the street and I noticed you because you were wearing a hat that said acid on it. And I thought, "Oh, that's a cool hat."
phrases.ja: 道を歩いてたら君に気づいた。アシッドって帽子をかぶってたから。いい帽子だな、って。

phrases.en: And I was like, "That guy's wearing a cool hat." And then I was like, "Oh, it's you." And then I had Moonshape Pool playing in my headphones and I stopped it and was like, "Oh, hello."
phrases.ja: いい帽子の人だな、って。それから、あ、君だ、って。ヘッドフォンで『A Moon Shaped Pool』がかかってて、止めて、やあ、って。

phrases.en: - Mr. York. - Mr. York. - Hello. I was impressed. - And you said, "Oh, hi." And then - - No, I said, "What the fuck?"
phrases.ja: ヨークさん。ヨークさん。こんにちは。感心したよ。君は「やあ」って。いや、僕は「なんだよ」って言った。

phrases.en: - Yeah. And - Then - Are you doing standing in the street? - And then I came to the show and then we met kind of properly at the show.
phrases.ja: うん。それで、道に立って何してるの？ それからショーに行って、ショーでちゃんと会った。

phrases.en: - Yeah. I didn't know you were living in Rome a lot. I had no idea. So I was double confused.
phrases.ja: うん。ローマにそんなに住んでるなんて知らなかった。全然。だから二重に混乱した。

phrases.en: - Yeah, it was really like, I think for me, through that and then the show, it always been, you to me had always been that person I was kind of scared of meeting.
phrases.ja: うん、本当に。僕には、あのこととショーを通して、君はずっと、会うのがちょっと怖い人だった。

phrases.en: - Oh yeah, I've got a whole list. - Yeah, totally. And I remember feeling so light afterwards, I think of just, oh, people and they're kind and they're nice.
phrases.ja: ああ、僕にもリストがある。うん、まったく。あとですごく軽くなったのを覚えてる。人って優しくて、いい人なんだ、って。

phrases.en: And it was very nice. - I was also impressed that you were just walking down the street. I was like, where's this security?
phrases.ja: すごくよかった。君がただ道を歩いてるのも感心した。警備はどこ、って。

phrases.en: Because I mean, I know I can do it. I didn't know you could do it. Is that a choice?
phrases.ja: 僕はできるって分かってる。君ができるとは知らなかった。それ、選んでるの？

phrases.en: - In the early days when I was in the band and stuff, so much of the hotel experience felt very locked in.
phrases.ja: バンドの初期とか、ホテルはすごく閉じ込められてた。

phrases.en: It felt like there was this like, oh, it's not safe for me to be out in some way. Yeah, that - Makes sense.
phrases.ja: 外に出るのは、なんか安全じゃない、みたいな感じ。うん、それは分かる。

phrases.en: - And then I remember I had a girlfriend who was very outgoing and she was coming to London and I was kind of like, oh
phrases.ja: それから、すごく外向的な彼女がロンドンに来ることになって、

phrases.en: if we just sit in my house for three days, she's going to think I'm nuts. So we kind of walked everywhere and it was this realization for me of like, oh, it's fine to be outside.
phrases.ja: 家に3日いたら、僕がおかしいと思われる、って。だからどこでも歩いた。外にいていいんだ、って気づいた。

phrases.en: It kind of broke that thing. And then now it's changed my life in such a big way. It's like how you stay connected to the world and the experience.
phrases.ja: それが壊れた。今は人生がすごく変わった。世界や経験と、つながり続ける方法みたいに。

phrases.en: And I read something about walking being the artist's kind of perspective because you're at ground level and you see things that you just don't see if you're driving - Everywhere.
phrases.ja: 歩くのはアーティストの視点だ、って読んだ。地面の高さにいるから、車だと見えないものが見える。どこでも。

phrases.en: It's also a good way to write. I wrote Wolf at the Door. I was going through a really bad moment and I walked for like two and a half days, rain, didn't matter.
phrases.ja: 書くのにもいい。『Wolf at the Door』はそう書いた。すごく悪い時期で、2日半くらい歩いた。雨でも関係なく。

phrases.en: A notebook in my hand and just wrote all and I felt so much better at the end of it. But also it's not just the walking, it's the walking past people.
phrases.ja: ノートを手に、全部書いた。終わりにはすごく楽になった。でも歩くだけじゃない。人の横を通り過ぎること。

phrases.en: The simple thing of people watching, playing that game of imagining as someone walks by where they're going, what they're doing, all that stuff brings you out of yourself
phrases.ja: 人を見る、あの単純なこと。通り過ぎる人がどこへ行くか、何をしてるか想像する。それが自分の外に出してくれる。

phrases.en: brings you out of your troubles. I mean, without it, See, it's really easy to get lost without being able to do that.
phrases.ja: 悩みの外へ。それがないと、本当に迷子になりやすい。

phrases.en: I guess I had a similar thing, but it happened for you very young, happened for me later. But I remember when we were on tour with REM and Michael Stipe figuring out that...
phrases.ja: 似たことはあった。君はすごく若いときに起きて、僕はあとだった。REMのツアーで、マイケル・スタイプが気づいた。

phrases.en: I mean, well, it was kind of obvious because when we played, I would just hide in the dressing room before them and never went out anywhere or whatever.
phrases.ja: Obviousだった。僕らが出るとき、僕は彼らの前、楽屋に隠れて、どこにも出なかった。

phrases.en: So he started dragging me out and he gave me this trick. He said, "If you don't care, they don't care. If you're not looking, they're not looking."
phrases.ja: だから引っ張り出されて、技をもらった。気にしなきゃ、向こうも気にしない。見てなきゃ、見られない、って。

phrases.en: And it works. I remember being in Stockholm going to some really busy club and he said, "Try it." And it works and nobody bothered us. So there are moments when you will feel vulnerable.
phrases.ja: 効くんだ。ストックホルムの、すごく混んだクラブで「やってみろ」って。効いて、誰も構ってこなかった。傷つきやすい瞬間はある。

phrases.en: There are moments when shit will happen or the sun will be printing your picture one too many times and you'll not want it or something. And I've had that.
phrases.ja: ひどいことが起きる瞬間もある。写真を刷られすぎて、もう嫌になるとか。僕もあった。

phrases.en: It's not an easy decision to make, but it's better than the alternative.
phrases.ja: 簡単な決断じゃない。でも、もう一方よりはいい。

phrases.en: The alternative, I know people who got death threats and then wouldn't leave the house and had security patrolling their house to hold all that sort of stuff.
phrases.ja: もう一方は、殺害予告を受けて家から出られなくなって、警備が家を巡回する。そういうの全部。

phrases.en: You don't want that. I think if you have something that's very successful, there's a lot of pressure to repeat that, which I'm sure you'll probably feel or you do feel sometimes.
phrases.ja: それは嫌だ。すごく当たったものがあると、それを繰り返せ、って圧力が大きい。君も感じるだろうし、ときどき感じてると思う。

phrases.en: It doesn't sort of go anywhere because that's like working to commission. You know what I mean? It's like we like those. Let's paint that - Again. - Yeah.
phrases.ja: それはどこにも行かない。注文仕事みたいだから。分かる？ あれが好きだった。もう一回それを描いて。うん。

phrases.en: Could you do that? I remember some movies, some being drawn in to watch some clip of the movie, "We'd really like you to do something like this."
phrases.ja: できる？ 映画の一部を見せられて、こういうのをやってほしい、って引き込まれるのを覚えてる。

phrases.en: And I was like, "Use that." That sort of mentality of like, "We want your name at the top, but we'd like you to repeat yourself, but
phrases.ja: それを使え、って。名前は一番上に欲しい。でも自分を繰り返してほしい。

phrases.en: we don't want to ask you to repeat yourself because we know it's rude. So we're kind of thinking about it's commercial art form, so therefore you're always going to get people asking you to do that."
phrases.ja: 繰り返せとは言いたくない。失礼だと分かってるから。商業のアートだから、いつもそう頼まれる、って考えてる。

phrases.en: - It's an interesting cycle, I think, because you make something that I think connects with people because they find something in it that you've captured something about the human experience, whether it's a
phrases.ja: 面白い循環だと思う。人とつながるものを作る。人がその中に、人間の経験の何かを見つけるから。

phrases.en: vulnerability or a sensitivity that comes with being human. And then I think any kind of success around that thing makes it take on this life of its own.
phrases.ja: 弱さとか、人間でいることの繊細さ。それから成功が、それに勝手な命を与える。

phrases.en: Then everything around you kind of makes your experience incredibly not human and then moving - - Yes, artificial. - Yeah.
phrases.ja: 周りの全部が、経験をものすごく人間じゃなくする。それから動いていく。うん、作り物。うん。

phrases.en: And then it feels like the kind of goal is to how do you shut that out when you're making stuff so that you can still be making stuff about the human experience.
phrases.ja: ものを作るとき、それをどう遮って、まだ人間の経験について作れるか、が目標みたいになる。

phrases.en: I've always thought if I was to make music about being in a studio and touring and all of the kind of shiny things that come with that and how wonderful that is -
phrases.ja: スタジオやツアーや、ついてくるキラキラについて音楽を作ったら、っていつも思ってた。それがどれだけ素晴らしいか。

phrases.en: It's - Shiny for you, mate. It's - Not shiny very well. It's definitely not interesting to me, so it can't possibly be interesting to anyone else.
phrases.ja: 君にはキラキラだよ。あんまりキラキラしてない。僕には全然面白くない。だから他の人にも面白いはずがない。

phrases.en: What I love about your work, for example, is for so many people who look at you in this way of in this kind of godlike status in terms of a creative - And
phrases.ja: 君の仕事が好きなのは、たくさんの人が、創造の神みたいに君を見てるのに。そして

phrases.en: - An artist to still be someone who kind of looks at, oh, this is the gritty part of life.
phrases.ja: アーティストなのに、まだ、これが人生のざらついた部分だ、って見てる人でいること。

phrases.en: I think that's what's so impressive about so much of your work is that for people to revere you in such a way - And to - Still be looking at what's under the
phrases.ja: それがすごいところだと思う。あんなに崇められて、まだ爪の下を見てる。

phrases.en: fingernails rather than... - All I can think is I think the reason for that was it's as much having to learn quite a difficult lesson.
phrases.ja: 爪の下を。それより上じゃなくて。思えるのは、かなり難しい教訓を学ばなきゃいけなかったからだ、ってこと。

phrases.en: And if you have to do lots of interviews, for example, if you end up having to explain your work in a particular way, when people are like...
phrases.ja: インタビューをたくさんやらなきゃ、仕事を決まった説明の仕方で説明することになる。人が…

phrases.en: You can get picked apart and what you've done can get picked apart in a way, which is what you mean by artificial, I think really, in a way that's not necessary.
phrases.ja: ばらされる。やったことが、ある意味ばらされる。それが君の言う作り物だと思う。必要ない形で。

phrases.en: I mean, it used to be a lot worse. Now I guess it's not as bad, but around kiddo amnesia, before that, I really struggled.
phrases.ja: 昔の方がずっと悪かった。今はそこまでじゃない。でもKid Aのあたり、その前は本当に苦しかった。

phrases.en: Every time I had to try to do something new, I was explaining it to myself while I was doing it, literally. It's like a form of madness and I couldn't get out of it.
phrases.ja: 新しいことをやるたびに、やりながら自分に説明してた。文字通り。狂気の一種で、抜けられなかった。

phrases.en: The experience of trying to make music, even the experience of being in the studio or listening back to stuff became this really weird hollow thing because I felt I needed to justify it
phrases.ja: 音楽を作ること、スタジオにいること、聴き返すことまで、変な空洞になった。正当化しなきゃ、って感じたから。

phrases.en: somehow, but not justify it in a sort of apologize, justify it in a kind of intellectual way. And the reason for that was I needed to get out of it.
phrases.ja: 謝る正当化じゃなくて、頭で正当化する。理由は、そこから出なきゃいけなかったから。

phrases.en: I needed to just get out of the studio and I needed to just walk. A lot of that was down to the fact that nobody cares, man.
phrases.ja: スタジオを出て、ただ歩かなきゃ。多くは、誰も気にしてない、ってことだった。

phrases.en: Nobody cares that it's difficult. And so if you're worried, if you're bummed out that it's difficult, fucking stop, go and do something else.
phrases.ja: 誰も、難しいことなんて気にしない。難しいって落ち込んでるなら、やめろ。他のことをしろ。

phrases.en: Also, later on as you have kids and all this kind of thing, the choice to carry on doing this kind of work, you have to enjoy it.
phrases.ja: 子どもができたりすると、この仕事を続けるには、楽しさが要る。

phrases.en: And the enjoyment comes from having to start again from scratch every time you start again, whatever you learn, you've got to unlearn or all this kind of nonsense.
phrases.ja: 楽しさは、始めるたびにゼロからやり直すことから来る。学んだことは、学び直さなきゃいけない。そういう話。

phrases.en: Also, songwriting is a very odd... I mean, going to the Ivan Novellos thing, I mean, I don't hang out with songwriters, but apparently I am one. And you realize that actually songwriting is quite a naive thing.
phrases.ja: 曲作りはすごく変で。アイヴァー・ノヴェロの話に行くと、ソングライターとはつるまない。でもどうやら僕はそうらしい。曲作りは、かなり無邪気なことだと分かる。

phrases.en: It's like you can't be savvy about it. You can work really hard on it, but the good stuff just happens and you don't know why.
phrases.ja: 抜け目なくはできない。すごく働ける。でもいいものは、ただ起きる。なぜか分からない。

phrases.en: And you've got to be honest with yourself that you don't know why, and you've got to carry on being honest with yourself that you don't know why.
phrases.ja: なぜか分からない、って自分に正直でいなきゃ。分からないまま、正直でい続けなきゃ。

phrases.en: And when stuff forms that you like, you just grab onto it and you don't let it go because the stuff you like is you don't know why you like it.
phrases.ja: 好きな形ができたら、掴んで離さない。好きなものは、なぜ好きか分からないから。

phrases.en: Why would Pyramid Song... I mean, it's three chords over and over again and the same lyric. How does that make sense?
phrases.ja: なぜ『Pyramid Song』が。コード3つを繰り返して、歌詞も同じ。なんで成立するんだ？

phrases.en: That kind of thing. But you like it, you like it. You're not bothered about if anyone else likes it.
phrases.ja: そういうこと。でも好きなんだ。好きなんだ。他の人が好きかどうかは気にしない。

phrases.en: - I've always wondered if part of that is why the idea of imposter syndrome that can come with commercial success exists is I think if you write in that way
phrases.ja: ずっと不思議だった。商業的な成功についてくる、偽物みたいな感じの一部は、そういう書き方だからじゃないか、って。

phrases.en: there's a part of you that kind of acknowledges... It almost feels like you're not responsible for it.
phrases.ja: 一部は認めてる。自分が責任を持ってないみたいに感じる。

phrases.en: So then if people are like, "Oh, you've made this thing and that means that you're this," there's something in there that feels like, "Oh, I can't take credit for it.
phrases.ja: 人が「これを作った、だから君はこれだ」って言うと、功績は受け取れない、って感じがある。

phrases.en: It just kind of happened to me."
phrases.ja: ただ、僕に起きただけ、って。

phrases.en: I think I've always found the things that I end up liking the most or have been the most special things to me are the ones where you kind of write it and then
phrases.ja: いちばん好きになるもの、いちばん特別なものは、書いてから、

phrases.en: as you're listening back or reading lyrics back, you're kind of learning something about yourself of you're realizing that you've said something rather than I'm going to sit down, I'm going to say this.
phrases.ja: 聴き返したり歌詞を読み返したりして、自分について何かを学んでるものだ。これを言おう、と座って言うんじゃなくて、言ってしまったことに気づく。

phrases.en: Yeah. - And you might not realize and you might record it and track it and everything and not realize until you've mastered it. Yeah. And then you suddenly hear, "Oh shit, that's what I - Meant."
phrases.ja: うん。気づかないこともある。録って、全部やって、マスタリングするまで気づかない。うん。それから「くそ、これが言いたかったことだ」って。

phrases.en: Yeah. - Yeah, that's right. I think, but at the same time, it's not not you because you spend... It's not divine intervention or anything like that. It's like you got to show up.
phrases.ja: うん。うん、その通り。でも同時に、君じゃないわけじゃない。時間をかけてるから。神が降りてくるとかじゃない。出てこなきゃいけない。

phrases.en: In order to find these things, you have to show up. Much like with any job, you develop skills at what you do. If you're a cameraman, you develop skills, you develop a relationship with your camera.
phrases.ja: 見つけるには、出てこなきゃ。どんな仕事でも同じ。腕がつく。カメラマンなら、カメラとの関係ができる。

phrases.en: If you are a songwriter, you develop a relationship with whatever the hell that is.
phrases.ja: ソングライターなら、それが何であれ、それとの関係ができる。

phrases.en: You have to learn to accept the months of imposter syndrome where you're like, "I don't have anything to justify all this amazing equipment in my studio. I can't find anything I like.
phrases.ja: 偽物みたいな感じの何ヶ月かを受け入れなきゃ。スタジオのすごい機材を正当化するものが何もない。好きなものが見つからない。

phrases.en: That's okay." And then you'll pick up your notebook or whatever and there'll be one line in it that sets you off. But the point is you showed up because it's really easy not to show up.
phrases.ja: それでいい。ノートを拾うと、一行があって、それが火をつける。要点は、出てきたこと。出てこないのは本当に簡単だから。

phrases.en: It's really easy to go, "Oh, I'll get to that one. Oh, I know what I'm doing. It's fine." Because it's the small acts that end up being the big acts.
phrases.ja: あとでやる、何をしてるか分かってる、大丈夫、は簡単。小さいことが、大きいことになるから。

phrases.en: It's really easy to get into this kind of mentality that everything is a performance where it's not everything is searching, in fact, and searching for stuff that speaks to you, not anybody else.
phrases.ja: 全部がパフォーマンスだ、って考えに入りやすい。実際は全部が探すこと。自分に話しかけるものを探す。他の誰かじゃない。

phrases.en: - Someone wants to describe it to me as kind of like surfing where you can practice getting up on the board and the waves are kind of going and sometimes you'll be practicing,
phrases.ja: 誰かがサーフィンに例えた。ボードに立つ練習はできる。波は来てる。ときどき練習してても、

phrases.en: but there's no waves. And then if a wave comes but you haven't practiced enough, you're not going to be able to surf it. That's right.
phrases.ja: 波がない。波が来ても、練習が足りないと乗れない。その通り。

phrases.en: And - Then - When they kind of happen, it's like the combination of you've practiced being able to capture it and it's something is happening at the right time.
phrases.ja: それが起きるときは、掴む練習をしてきて、正しいタイミングで何かが起きてる。

phrases.en: - Yeah, you're ready when it's... Yeah. - And that's when it's like - - Or if I'm surfing, you're not ready ever or you're on the rock scope.
phrases.ja: うん、準備ができてるとき。うん。それが、みたいな。僕がサーフィンしてたら、いつまでも準備できないか、岩の上にいる。

phrases.en: Just - Like being open. And I think I used to feel really... I've had a big shift away from... I think I used to feel really labor focused about art in general.
phrases.ja: ただ開いてること。昔はアートを、労働で測ってた。大きな変化があった。

phrases.en: If it was walking in and seeing a painting and doing that like, "Oh, that can't have taken more than 10 minutes or whatever."
phrases.ja: 絵を見て、これ、10分もかかってないだろ、みたいな。

phrases.en: And I felt like to justify it, I had to be in the studio for months at a time and just in there. - That's your imposter syndrome speaking.
phrases.ja: 正当化するには、何ヶ月もスタジオにいなきゃ、って感じた。ただそこに。それは偽物みたいな声が話してる。

phrases.en: Yeah. Because that's how... I'm the same. Yeah.
phrases.ja: うん。そういうことだから。僕も同じ。うん。

phrases.en: I mean, sometimes it's fun, but sometimes you're like you're doing it because you feel you should do it because you need to stay ahead of the game or you need to keep proving
phrases.ja: 楽しいときもある。でも、やるべきだからやってるときがある。先を行かなきゃ、とか、

phrases.en: that you are who you say you are.
phrases.ja: 自分が言う自分だって証明し続けなきゃ、って。

phrases.en: I mean, there are good sides to it, but there's a point where it just doesn't give you anything back and it can really freak you out because you've been there for weeks and
phrases.ja: いい面もある。でも何も返ってこなくなる点がある。何週間もいて、

phrases.ja: 昔はそう思ってた。今は、この曲を歌うために深く掘る必要はないと思う。逆だ。

phrases.en: You need to just totally let go and go, "If I'm not feeling this right now I'm good with that because maybe in 10 minutes it's going to really hit me like a train," which often it does.
phrases.ja: 完全に手放して、今これを感じてなくても、それでいい。10分後に電車みたいに来るかもしれない。よくそうなる。

phrases.en: - You have so many moments in your life, I think everyone does, where you have those songs, if you like music at all, where
phrases.ja: 人生には、そういう瞬間がすごく多い。音楽が好きなら、みんなそうだと思う。

phrases.en: you're like, "Oh, this is also a song or this is also a movie or something." I remember seeing Pulp Fiction for the first time and being like, "Oh, this is a film as well."
phrases.ja: あ、これも曲なんだ、とか、これも映画なんだ。『パルプ・フィクション』を初めて見たとき、あ、これも映画なんだ、って。

phrases.en: And hearing Shine on You Crazy Diamond for the first time and being so confused by it that this was a song and that was what you could do also.
phrases.ja: 『Shine On You Crazy Diamond』を初めて聴いて、これが曲で、こういうこともできるんだ、って混乱した。

phrases.en: With the Carmen Police video, for example, I remember watching that and being like, "Oh, this is so brilliant." I feel like so much of your music has that weight where it really, you just remember hearing it.
phrases.ja: 『Karma Police』のビデオも、見て、これはすごい、って。君の音楽の多くには、その重さがある。聴いたことを本当に覚えてる。

phrases.en: It's all so different from each other in a way that is, I think, so inspiring just to see someone be so consistently great in so many different ways, but
phrases.ja: 互いにとても違って、それが刺激になる。こんなに違う形で、こんなにずっとすごい人を見ること。

phrases.en: in so many different ways. It can be hard to timeline it sometimes in terms of... There's not this obvious like, "Well, it was this, then it was this, then it was this, then it was this."
phrases.ja: こんなに違う形で。順番にするのが難しいときがある。これがこう、それからこれ、が明らかじゃない。

phrases.en: It's all its own thing in a way that I think just makes it feel so fresh always. I've just always really been drawn to stuff like... I love Codex or True Love White or something.
phrases.ja: 全部がそれ自身で、いつも新しく感じる。ずっと惹かれてきた。『Codex』とか『True Love Waits』とかが好き。

phrases.en: Yeah. I just have always loved that sort of... I mean, everything in its right place is it for me. It's always been so much of that. I mean, I find it so inspiring.
phrases.ja: うん。ずっとあの感じが好き。『Everything in Its Right Place』は、僕にとってはそれ。ずっとそう。すごく刺激になる。

phrases.en: - Everything's right place was my response to not being out right. We had this empty house, we had a grand piano, we had a mattress. That's the first thing I did when we moved into this house.
phrases.ja: あれは、外に出てないことへの返事だった。空き家があって、グランドピアノがあって、マットレスがあった。この家に引っ越して最初にやったこと。

phrases.en: I mean, finding lost, felt lost ever since that okay can be a thing. And when I found that, okay, weirdly with that one, it was like a mantra.
phrases.ja: 迷子を見つけて、あれ以来、大丈夫であり得る、って感じた。あれは、奇妙に、唱える言葉みたいだった。

phrases.en: I wasn't thinking, oh, I'm writing a song. I was just really enjoying playing piano in this empty house. And I had one CD, which was a and that's it.
phrases.ja: 曲を書いてる、とは思ってなかった。空き家でピアノを弾くのを、ただ楽しんでた。CDは一枚だけ。それだけ。

phrases.en: And it was during the winter and there was storms all the time and just had a mattress. It was so great. Just playing this riff over and over and over again to make myself feel better.
phrases.ja: 冬で、いつも嵐で、マットレスだけ。最高だった。気分をよくするために、このリフを何度も何度も。

phrases.en: I love that thing of, it arrives in the post, you plug it in, you don't read the manual, you just start messing about and you find something
phrases.ja: 郵便で届いて、挿して、説明書は読まない。いじり始めて、何かを見つける、あの感じが好き。

phrases.en: whether it's a synth or a drum machine or guitar or anything.
phrases.ja: シンセでも、ドラムマシンでも、ギターでも。

phrases.en: Establishing a relationship with this construction, this thing and responding to it and responding to what people thought you might like about it, what you don't like about it, all this stuff.
phrases.ja: この機械、このものと関係を作る。反応する。人が好きかもしれないと思うものにも、嫌いなものにも。全部。

phrases.en: I've got so much out of that kind of process over the years that I figured that it must be part of what writing is, part of what our particular process is.
phrases.ja: 何年も、あの過程からすごく多くを得た。書くことの一部、僕らのやり方の一部なんだ、って分かった。

phrases.en: There are just some days when nothing happened and then some days you'll pick up something you're unfamiliar with and the unfamiliarity means you have to make a sort of step
phrases.ja: 何も起きない日もある。知らないものを拾う日もある。知らないから、一歩を踏み出さなきゃいけない。

phrases.en: you have to step across. And that stepping across means like, okay, I don't know why I like what's happening here and the I don't know why I like thing is what music should be, which
phrases.ja: 向こう側に出なきゃ。その一歩は、ここで起きてることがなぜ好きか分からない。なぜ好きか分からない、が音楽であるべきこと。

phrases.en: is why strangely enough, algorithms don't produce an awful lot of that.
phrases.ja: だから奇妙に、アルゴリズムはそれをあまり生まない。

phrases.en: The human creativity is kind of like the same kind of thing as a scientist trying to solve a problem and he has all the things set up and he's gone
phrases.ja: 人間が作ることは、問題を解こうとする科学者と同じ種類だ。全部並べて、

phrases.en: he's tried everything and he can't figure it out. He's in the same kind of place, right? He's in the like, where I'm lost now, I've tried everything.
phrases.ja: 全部試して、分からない。同じ場所にいる。今は迷子だ。全部試した。

phrases.en: And then he goes away and he sleeps on it and he comes back and then something clicks. Because why?
phrases.ja: それから離れて、寝て、戻ってきて、何かがカチッとなる。なぜ？

phrases.en: Because he's unfamiliar, because he can't make sense or something and then he can or she suddenly makes sense, something falls into place.
phrases.ja: 知らないから。意味が作れないから。それから急に意味が通る。何かがはまる。

phrases.en: - For me, it's just kind of where the risk falls is kind of inverted on itself of where you think it might be.
phrases.ja: 僕にとっては、リスクが落ちる場所が、思う場所と逆になってる。

phrases.en: Someone else might feel like trying something different feels really risky in some way or straying from what people like about your music feels like a risky thing.
phrases.ja: 違うことを試すのが怖い人もいる。人が好きなことから外れるのが怖い。

phrases.en: But I think the trying to recreate for that reason is that's the risky thing. - That's just awful. - That to me is the terrifying part, the idea of doing that.
phrases.ja: でもその理由で同じものを作り直すのが、怖いことだと思う。それはただ最悪。僕にとって怖いのは、それをする考え。

phrases.en: And I think any time... Sometimes there's songs that we've done in the studio and you finish it and you're like, "I think this is a great song.
phrases.ja: スタジオで曲を終えて、これはいい曲だと思う。

phrases.en: I think it's really good." But it doesn't excite me at all. Maybe because it has something that reminds you of something else you've done or whatever it is that it's just - I should like this.
phrases.ja: 本当にいい。でも全然興奮しない。他にやった何かを思い出させるから、とか。ただ、これは好きであるべきだ。

phrases.en: You're not learning anything. I should - Like this. Yeah. I - Should like this. I should like it, but you just don't. And - - I mean, I had that with Codex all the way through it.
phrases.ja: 何も学んでない。これは好きであるべき。うん。好きであるべき。好きであるべきなのに、ただ好きじゃない。『Codex』はずっとそれだった。

phrases.en: The rest of the band forced me personally to finish it. Everyone was like, "You're fucking crazy, man." I'm like, "All right. So sometimes..."
phrases.ja: バンドの残りが、僕に仕上げさせた。みんな、狂ってるぞ、って。分かった。ときどき。

phrases.en: - For me, at least so much of the studio experience of making something is almost trying to block out the fact that anyone's going to listen to it for a second to just
phrases.ja: 僕にとっては、何かを作るスタジオの多くは、誰かが聴く、って事実を一瞬でも閉め出そうとすること。

phrases.en: make what - It is. You're doing it for you. - Yeah. You have to just be making what do I want to listen to at this time in my life?
phrases.ja: それであるものを作る。自分のためにやってる。うん。今の人生で、自分が聴きたいものを作らなきゃ。

phrases.en: What is it that I feel like I want to do, say, make? And the fact that people are going to hear it feels like that happens late.
phrases.ja: やりたい、言いたい、作りたいと感じるものは何？ 人が聴く、って事実は、あとで起きる感じ。

phrases.en: The realization of that feels like it happens later. And I think the live playing music to an audience is the part where you're embracing the fact that people listen to it and that it's connected with people.
phrases.ja: その気づきは、あと。ライブで人にやるのは、人が聴いて、人とつながった、ってことを受け入れる部分。

phrases.en: And I think for me, the kind of emotion that happened at the end of the London shows was like...
phrases.ja: ロンドンのショーの終わりに来た感情は、僕には。

phrases.en: I think it was just a realization of that those shows felt so much to me like a culmination of so many people's support, I think. I think that's the bit.
phrases.ja: すごく多くの人の支えが、一つに集まったみたいに感じた。そこだと思う。

phrases.en: That part feels so external. I think you make the thing, and then how many shows you play is determined by how many people want to come see it.
phrases.ja: その部分は、すごく外にある。ものを作る。何本やるかは、見に来たい人の数で決まる。

phrases.en: And I think what - Was - Turns out a - Lot. What was emotional for me was it felt... I was kind of realizing, I think, how deep it is and how deeper it is
phrases.ja: 結果、たくさんだった。僕にとって感情的だったのは、気づいてたんだと思う。どれだけ深いか。

phrases.en: how much deeper it is than kind of any one moment or one song or any sort of fluke thing.
phrases.ja: 一つの瞬間や、一曲や、まぐれより、どれだけ深いか。

phrases.en: It just felt like supported kind of in a way more than like, "We're here because we want to hear this song that you've done
phrases.ja: 支えられてる感じだった。この曲を聴きたいから来た、より、

phrases.en: or we're here because we like when you used to play that one, or it just felt like we're here because we believe in what you're doing." And I think that's what it felt like to me.
phrases.ja: 昔あの曲をやってたのが好きだから、より、やってることを信じてるから来てる、感じ。僕にはそう感じた。

phrases.en: And I think that's why I found it so emotional was I think... - Also, you have to give a lot of yourself. You have to give a lot of yourself, and that makes you very open.
phrases.ja: だから感情的だった。あと、自分をたくさん渡さなきゃいけない。たくさん渡す。それでとても開く。

phrases.en: I've heard people say to me, "Careful with that, because you're exposed to all these people and all this kind of thing." And like, "Yeah, it doesn't bother me.
phrases.ja: 気をつけろ、こんな人たち、こんなものに晒される、って言われた。うん、気にならない。

phrases.en: Did, it did. It did. Used to. It doesn't bother me anymore." - I mean, I think if you're sensitive enough to want to write, sensitive enough to be aware of the part of you that wants to say anything
phrases.ja: 昔は気になった。昔は。もう気にならない。書くほど敏感なら、何かを言いたい部分に気づくほど敏感なら、

phrases.en: if you're sensitive enough to care enough about a song to be like, "It's not right yet.
phrases.ja: 曲を気にするほど敏感なら、まだ正しくない、って。

phrases.en: I have this idea and I want it to be right and I want it to be great," there's a sensitivity there that needs it to be great.
phrases.ja: このアイデアがあって、正しくしたい。すごくしたい。そこには、すごくある必要がある繊細さがある。

phrases.en: And I think if you're sensitive enough to do that, to feel it and then to communicate it and then see it through put so much of your life into making sure this synth sound is correct
phrases.ja: それを感じるほど敏感なら、伝えて、最後まで見て、このシンセの音が正しいように人生の多くを入れるなら、

phrases.en: then I think you're sensitive enough to feel when those moments land on you in what might come back at you.
phrases.ja: その瞬間が自分に着地するとき、返ってくるものを感じるほど、敏感だと思う。

phrases.en: I think a lot of the time when you're making stuff, you're kind of trying to reject what's coming back at you to remain sort of beginner's mind of how do I go back
phrases.ja: ものを作ってるとき、多くは、返ってくるものを拒もうとしてる。初めての気持ちを残すために。

phrases.en: to before anyone liked this song that I did or anything like that. You're always trying to get back to a sense of starting again.
phrases.ja: この曲が好きになる前に戻るには、って。いつも、また始める感じに戻ろうとしてる。

phrases.en: So I think those moments where you kind of let go and open up and allow it all to come in and you get to feel that
phrases.ja: だから手放して、開いて、全部を入れさせて、それを感じる瞬間は、

phrases.en: I think it is a wave of something that you don't live with every day. So it's quite - Like - You certainly don't, bro.
phrases.ja: 毎日一緒にいない波だと思う。だからかなり。君は確かに、そうじゃないよ。

phrases.en: I guess if I was going to answer that I'd say when we did the first radio show in Madrid, we had to do this thing where we had to walk through the audience.
phrases.ja: それに答えるなら、マドリードで最初のラジオのショーをしたとき、客の中を歩かなきゃいけなかった。

phrases.en: Never done that before. Walk through the audience and we had to stand on the stage getting prepped before we went up, up.
phrases.ja: やったことがなかった。客の中を歩いて、上がる前にステージで準備した。

phrases.en: The first time we did that after, I don't know how many years, all of us, the whole band were like, "Okay, keep it together. Keep it together."
phrases.ja: 何年かぶりにそれをやったあと、全員が、大丈夫、持ちこたえて、って。

phrases.en: Because I just wanted to... I already wanted to burst into tears because I hadn't been exposed to whatever that was for so long and to walk through the middle of it and then I never forget it.
phrases.ja: もう泣き出したかった。あんなに長く、あれに触れてなかった。真ん中を歩いて、忘れない。

phrases.en: I mean, all of us, we were like, "Holy shit. Holy shit." Also, you mentioned Beginner's Mind. Do you know the book?
phrases.ja: 全員、なんてことだ、なんてことだ、って。初心の心にも触れた。あの本、知ってる？

phrases.en: - Yeah. - The Suzuki book. Okay, good. Very important. - Very important. Which brings us back to walking the artist's perspective where we began. There's the bow, there's the seal.
phrases.ja: うん。鈴木の本。分かった、いい。すごく大事。すごく大事。それで、始めたところに戻る。歩くこと、アーティストの視点。お辞儀があって、締めがある。
